crit: Twenty multi-class data sets are used, the first 10 without class-imbalance and the remaining ones imbalanced (14 UCI, 6 synthetic); because it is interesting to see whether RESCALEnew works on imbalanced multi-class data, the class-imbalance experiment uses the ten imbalanced data sets. No other reason for the choice of data sets is given.
notes: Journal extension of the AAAI 2006 paper (same 20 data sets, same Table 2 values), with seven cost-sensitive learners; it says it extends the preliminary work (Zhou and Liu 2006a) but does not say the data list was taken from it, so benchmark_inherited_from is 'not stated in paper'. All data sets are multi-class with native class distributions; no binarisation, resizing or minority definition. The method-target reason is explicit only for the pure class-imbalance experiment (Section 4.4, Table 24); for the cost experiments the paper only describes the balanced/imbalanced split. connect4 and splice are excluded for the neural-network and ensemble learners, and splice for PETs, because of training cost (p.245, p.247, p.249). Synthetic sets are balanced. No IR column, no minority column, no SMOTE comparison.
